datasets: NIBRS Group A Crime Data (Open Baltimore 204beefe92a645d79fdf0969957bbdf8)
concurrency_primitives: goroutines, bounded channels, sync.WaitGroup; generic chunked worker pool with splitter/workers/closer/collector (internal/ingest/concurrent.go), buffer recycling via free channel, FNV-1a sharded concurrent join (internal/match/match.go), two-file parallel load (cmd/capstone/main.go); compare mode deep-equals sequential vs concurrent
design_patterns: Pipeline (ingest->match->aggregate->report, stages depend only on model), Strategy (report.Report interface, 5 question types), worker pool / fan-out fan-in, sharding by key
questions: Do neighborhoods with the most sanitation/dumping 311 requests also have the highest crime? (with all-311 baseline)
Top 10 neighborhoods by combined distress index (crime + resident 311 volume), by quarter
Are 311 requests closed more slowly in high-crime neighborhoods? (raw and mix-adjusted)
Do neighborhoods with many streetlight requests see more nighttime outdoor crime? (count and share)
Which neighborhoods have high 311 volume but low crime?
overview: Multi-package Go pipeline (ingest/match/aggregate/report over a shared model) with a generic chunked parallel CSV loader, sharded concurrent join, Strategy-pattern reports, and a compare mode that proves sequential and concurrent results are identical. Code is idiomatic modern Go, thoroughly commented, tested in every package, with CI; the README documents design, measurements and limitations and matches the code exactly.
stakeholder_value: The five questions are real cross-dataset analyses that control for neighborhood size (baselines, mix-adjusted close ratios, shares), so the Mayor's Office, DPW/DOT and BPD get honest, actionable answers (e.g., no service-speed penalty in high-crime areas once request mix is controlled; a stable 7-neighborhood distress shortlist). Joins on (neighborhood, month) are meaningful, not coincidental counting.
issues: No real data bundled; user must run two documented curl commands (verified working today). Program has no fetch mode.
go.mod requires go 1.27.2, forcing a toolchain download on older Go installs (documented).
Terminal-only visualization (ASCII tables/bars), no HTML or web UI.
29.5% of 311 rows lack a neighborhood and are dropped (documented).
rationale: Clean build, verified real data, full parallel parse and join with race-clean synchronization, documented and measured memory design, clean tested architecture, and five substantive cross-dataset questions earn full marks on seven criteria. Five points are deducted on real_data because the datasets are neither bundled nor fetched by the program; the user must download them with README-provided commands. 95/100, A.
